{{short description|Algebraic structure}}
In [[mathematics]], a (left) '''coherent ring''' is a [[ring (mathematics)|ring]] in which every [[Ideal_(ring_theory)#Types_of_ideals|finitely generated]] left [[ideal (ring theory)|ideal]] is [[finitely presented module|finitely presented]]. 

Many theorems about [[finitely generated module]]s over [[Noetherian ring]]s can be extended to finitely presented modules over coherent rings. 

Every left Noetherian ring is left coherent. The ring of [[polynomial]]s in an infinite number of variables over a left Noetherian ring is an example of a left coherent ring that is not left Noetherian.

A ring is left coherent [[if and only if]] every [[direct product]] of [[flat module|flat]] right [[module (mathematics)|modules]] is flat {{harv|Chase|1960}}, {{harv|Anderson|Fuller|1992|p=229}}.  Compare this to: A ring is left Noetherian if and only if every [[direct sum of modules|direct sum]] of [[injective module|injective]] left modules is injective.
